source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Severe brain injury can raise complex questions about prognosis and future care preferences, making thoughtful, supported family discussions valuable","B":"Advance directives being considered largely irrelevant to the ongoing care of a client with a severe brain injury of this kind","C":"Advance directive discussions applying mainly to clients who already have a pre-existing written directive on file","D":"This kind of conversation generally being avoided by the team unless the client themselves is able to participate directly"}}
source_row.rationale: Advance care planning discussions are important for families of clients with severe, potentially unrecoverable brain injury, since this situation can raise complex questions about prognosis and future care preferences, making thoughtful, well-supported family discussions valuable, particularly when the client cannot participate directly due to their condition, and whether or not a prior written directive exists.
source_row.source_detail: Supporting Families Through Advance Care Discussions
